login.description: Sign in to the device's panel.
login.resetHint: Holding the BOOT button for 10 s restores it.
settings.description: Device name, panel password and firmware update.
settings.name: Name
settings.nameHint: Shown in the panel and in Home Assistant. The network address is made from it.
settings.passwordHint: Protects the panel and the API. Scripts sign in with HTTP Basic (whisli:<password>). Holding BOOT for 10 s restores the default password.
settings.defaultPassword: You are using the default password – change it.
firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.hint: Upload a firmware.bin file. The device saves it and restarts; settings and buttons stay.
firmware.restartMessage: The device will be unavailable for a few seconds.
firmware.uploaded: Firmware saved, the device is restarting.
firmware.waiting: Waiting for the device to come back…
firmware.notBack: The device did not come back within a minute. Check its power and network.
network.description: The Wi-Fi connection and the access point for the first setup.
network.apHint: Turns on by itself when the device has no Wi-Fi for a minute. The panel is then at http://192.168.4.1/.
network.wifiHint: The network the device joins. Pick it from the list or type its name.
network.connectHint: After changing the network the device gets a new IP address. If it cannot connect, it opens the access point after a minute.
network.forgetMessage: The device disconnects from {ssid} and opens the access point {ap}.
network.apPasswordHint: Password of the {ssid} network. Default: whisli_gogo.
network.apDefaultPassword: The access point uses the default password – change it.
mqtt.description: Home Assistant over MQTT. The device works the same without a broker.
mqtt.connectionHint: The device connects to an MQTT broker – usually the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant – and announces itself there.
mqtt.baseTopicHint: Start of this device's topics. Leave empty for the default.
mqtt.discoveryPrefixHint: Where Home Assistant looks for devices. Usually “homeassistant”.
mqtt.discovery: Announce the device in Home Assistant (MQTT Discovery)
mqtt.topicsHint: Home Assistant creates the device by itself: Wi-Fi signal, an event entity and a trigger for every button with MQTT ticked.
diagnostics.description: State of the IR receiver and the chip – useful when looking for faults.
logs.description: The device's latest events (up to {capacity}). The log lives in RAM – a restart clears it.
error.invalidSsid: Enter the network name (up to 32 characters).
error.invalidTopic: Topic: no #, + or empty levels, up to 64 characters.
problem.mqtt: No connection to the MQTT broker.
mqttError.credentials: The broker rejected the user or password.
mqttError.unreachable: Cannot reach the server – check the address, port and network.
buttons.description: Remote buttons and what they do.
buttons.pressHint: Press a button on the remote.
buttons.none: No buttons yet. Add the first one.
buttons.deleteMessage: The button “{name}” leaves the database. You can learn it again.
buttons.changing: This remote sends something different every time. Air conditioner remotes work like this, and such a button cannot be learned.
buttons.unreadable: The signal arrives but is unreadable. Move closer and aim straight at the receiver.
buttons.name: Name
receiver.description: What the IR receiver sees, live. Useful when a remote does not work.
receiver.waitingHint: Aim a remote at the receiver and press a button.
receiver.unreadableFrame: The signal arrives, but the frame was unreadable.
receiver.stuckLowHint: Check the receiver’s power and wiring.
receiver.noFrameHint: Only short pulses so far. Check the remote and the receiver’s power.
error.invalidCode: A button code may hold only letters, digits and hyphens, up to 15 characters.
error.full: Memory full: too many buttons or actions.
error.saveFailed: Could not save to the device’s memory.
actions.insecure: Do not check the certificate (e.g. a local Home Assistant with its own certificate)
log.actionDropped: Too many presses at once, skipped {detail}
error.invalidAction: The chosen webhook or server no longer exists. Choose another.
mqtt.topicButton: a press of a button with MQTT ticked, as JSON: code, name, gesture
mqtt.topicEvent: the same for the event entity
mqtt.examplesHint: What Home Assistant receives, using a button called “{name}”. The topics are the real ones for this device.
mqtt.examplePressHint: Three messages for every gesture with MQTT ticked. The broker does not retain them.
mqtt.exampleTriggerHint: Retained by the broker. This is what makes the button appear in Home Assistant's automation editor.
learn.press: Press a button on the remote…
learn.pressHint: Aim the remote at the device.
learn.pressAgainHint: This remote has no checksum, so the code has to repeat.
edit.unsavedLeave: These changes cannot be saved yet. Leave anyway?
edit.deleteHint: It goes with its actions. You can learn it again.
actions.typeHint.wol: Wakes a chosen computer or server.
buttons.legend: The status shows the last run.
edit.needCode: Press a button on the remote and it saves by itself.
edit.needName: Enter a name and it saves by itself.
hooks.description: HTTP requests to Home Assistant, Node-RED or any server. Define them here, and buttons call them from their actions.
hooks.name: Name
hooks.headersHint: One per line, e.g. access tokens.
hooks.removeUsed: The webhook “{name}” is used in actions: {count}. Those actions will stop working and show an error.
error.invalidUrl: The URL must start with http:// or https://.
error.busy: Another test is running. Try again in a moment.
servers.description: Computers and servers a button can wake over the network. Wake-on-LAN must be enabled in their BIOS and system.
servers.sent: Packet sent to {address}. The device does not confirm receipt.
servers.broadcastHint: Empty: this network. Set it when the server is on another network or VLAN.
servers.removeUsed: The server “{name}” is used by buttons: {count}. That option will stop working and show an error.
edit.noHooks: No webhooks. Add the first one.
edit.noServers: No servers. Add the first one.
edit.pickHook: Choose a webhook or untick this option.
edit.pickServer: Choose a server or untick this option.
actions.typeHint.mqtt: Sends the button’s name and the type of press.
edit.longHint: Acts when the button has been down for 0.8 s.
edit.shortHint: Acts the moment the button is pressed.
edit.shortHintDelayed: Acts once the button is released, so with a slight delay, to tell it from a long press.
edit.onceHint: One event per hold, however long you hold.
edit.repeatHint: Repeats every 0.3 s while you hold. A webhook skips a repeat while the previous one is running, and Wake-on-LAN goes only once.
led.description: What the LED on the board shows. Changes apply at once.
led.mode.receivedHint: Flashes for every frame from a remote. Useful for aiming and checking range.
led.mode.sentHint: Flashes when a button really runs its actions.
led.mode.statusHint: Dark while all is well. A flash every 2 s means no Wi-Fi, every 3 s another problem, e.g. MQTT.
led.mode.offHint: Never lit, except for a password reset with the BOOT button.
led.alertsHint: A flash every 2 s means no Wi-Fi, every 3 s another problem, e.g. MQTT. Problems take priority over the mode.
edit.notePlaceholder: e.g. Turns on the living room lamp and dims the TV
